Youth-led, in the Philippines

Three words we hold close

Our name comes from them. They guide everything we do.

KamalayanAwareness

"Kamalayan" is the Filipino word for awareness. KaSoL raises awareness about the challenges faced by individuals awaiting trial, children in juvenile detention, and survivors of abuse, and provides support to these communities through additional aid and assistance.

SolusyonSolution

"Solusyon" is the Filipino word for solution. KaSoL hopes to be one of the many efforts contributing to positive change in the Philippine judiciary system.

LayaFreedom

"Laya" is the Filipino word for freedom, meaning to be free. KaSoL believes that easing the burdens on the current judicial system can create more space for growth and progress.

Join us

Who we are

KaSoL is a youth-driven organization that aims to fill in the gaps in existing services by providing additional support and assistance to individuals awaiting trial, children in juvenile detention, and survivors of abuse.

Our mission and values

Our tagline is also our promise. Here is what each word means to us.

KamalayanAwareness

We start by paying attention. Many people never hear about what life is like for those awaiting trial, for children in juvenile detention, or for survivors of abuse. We share their realities and offer extra aid and assistance where we can.

SolusyonSolution

We don't claim to fix everything. We hope to be one of the many efforts adding up to positive change in the Philippine judiciary system, one project at a time.

LayaFreedom

We believe in freedom: to grow, to heal, and to move forward. Easing the burdens on the current judicial system can create more space for growth and progress.

The issue, in plain words

Imagine waiting years for your day in court.

Right now, about 7 in 10 people in detention in the Philippines are still awaiting trial. As of June 2024, 171,247 Filipinos were in detention, and about 119,873 of them hadn't had their trial yet.

The courts are carrying a very heavy load, too. In November 2024, Senate President Pro Tempore Jinggoy Estrada reported 933,624 unresolved cases.

Behind every number is a person, and often a family waiting with them. That's why we show up with extra support, and why we keep sharing what we learn.

In partnership with the Women's Wellness and Crisis Center (WWCC), Parañaque City

Project Diwa

Project Diwa provides activities, excursions, and opportunities to earn income and build awareness for WEDC (Women in Especially Difficult Circumstances) at the Women's Crisis Center in Parañaque City.

About the WWCC

A home for WEDC, founded in 2019 and located on M. Rodriguez St., La Huerta, Parañaque City.

Services:

  • Social
  • Dietary
  • Homelife
  • Productivity
  • Medical
  • Psychological
  • Spiritual
  • Educational
  • After-care

Who are WEDC?

  • Women who are victims of physical, sexual, or psychological abuse
  • Victims of exploitation
  • Those involved in or rescued from illegal recruitment
  • Victims of armed conflict or displacement
  • Women with mental health conditions or disabilities
"To immediately provide temporary shelter and custodial care to Women in Especially Difficult Circumstances (WEDC) in need of protection and care. Through the delivery of programs and services, residents will be provided opportunities for healing and growth, ensuring a safe place for all."WCC mission

Why we hold these sessions

  • Give the women a way to process complicated emotions
  • Bring joy to their day-to-day lives
  • Offer an opportunity for income and livelihood
  • Better understand their needs

What a session looks like

  1. Opening remarks
  2. Icebreakers
  3. Activity with a lesson
  4. Clean-up
  5. Social time
  6. Closing and goodbyes

Things we make and do together

  • Scrapbooking
  • Jewelry making
  • Crocheting
  • Singing
  • Dancing
  • Bracelet and rosary making
  • Painting and self-expression
  • Letters to their future selves

Highlights so far

  1. Session 1

    • Icebreaker (human bingo)
    • Scrapbooking and goal setting

  2. Session 2

    • Bracelet, necklace, and headband making
    • Karaoke
    • A movie and Just Dance for the kids

  3. Session 3

    • Bracelet, rosary, and necklace making
    • Mask making and karaoke
    • Brainstorming an action plan

  4. Session 5

    • Updates on product sales
    • Brainstorming how to better reach markets
    • Painting and letters to their future selves

  5. Christmas outreach

    Gifts and a day out at Manila Zoo and Jollibee.

    Fundraising goal: ₱30,000, covering transportation, tickets, gifts, and food.

  6. Women's Day celebration at the WWCC

    A Jollibee treat, karaoke and dancing, a magic show, and gifts for the WWCC staff, in collaboration with the Keys Secondary Student Council.

    Theme: "Empowerment is Justice, and Justice is Empowerment. Women's Day should not be just today, but every single day."

  7. 7th anniversary celebration at the WWCC

    March 31, 2026

    A recognition ceremony with the WWCC head, team, partners, and donors. Held at Manila Zoo and Jollibee with WWCC members and fellow volunteers.

1 in 4

In the Philippines, 1 in 4 women aged 15–49 has experienced violence from a partner. In 2022, 17.5% of women reported physical, sexual, or emotional violence from current or recent partners. Women's centers provide shelter but face resource shortages, leaving women vulnerable to cycles of poverty and injustice.

In partnership with Kalipay and Iloilo City National High School

Project Kalayo

A youth workshop empowering kids ages 10–16 to find their voice, lead with kindness, and care for their communities.

Identity and self-expression

Vision boards, journaling, and playdough art to discover "Who am I?"

Leadership

Public speaking drills and collaboration activities.

Community awareness

Interactive activities connecting family, school, and barangay.

Why we do it

We want to teach leadership skills, promote active citizenship, and show that these kids are a force of change who can change their lives and their communities.

What happens at a workshop

  • Icebreakers and games
  • Identity sculptures
  • Journaling and art
  • Energizers
  • Community collage
  • Takeaways and reflection
  • Rights and responsibilities workshop
  • Public speaking drills
  • Project-making workshop
  • Commitment ceremony

Our partners

Kalipay

Kalipay has been a safe haven since 2007 for disadvantaged, homeless, abandoned, neglected, malnourished, and abused children and victims of child labor and trafficking, offering education, shelter, health care, and counseling.

Iloilo City National High School

Iloilo City National High School opened its doors to empower girls aged 11–16 by hosting the workshops.
